task.title: Cut pre-releases by exact version
task.description:
Let a release be cut as a pre-release, `vX.Y.Z-rcN`, by naming that exact version; nothing else about the stable release path changes.

Decided 2026-09-19 with Dylan: pre-releases are a manual act, never automated. A bump label or a bump kind can only ever produce a stable version, so the release pull request path is untouched and cannot cut a pre-release by accident. The first use is `v0.6.0-rc1`, to test the release path end to end before v0.6.0 is ready.

## The version grammar

A version is `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` (as today, no leading zeroes) optionally followed by `-rcN`, where N is a positive integer with no leading zero. `0.6.0-rc1` and `0.6.0-rc12` are versions; `0.6.0-rc`, `0.6.0-rc0`, `0.6.0-rc01`, `0.6.0-beta1`, `0.6.0-rc.1` are not. `-rcN` is the only pre-release form: one spelling keeps ordering trivial and keeps the tags readable beside the stable ones.

## Ordering

Neither `sort -V` nor `git tag --sort=v:refname` orders a pre-release before its stable version, so the release scripts stop relying on either and order versions themselves, in one place (`scripts/release-version.sh`):

- by MAJOR, MINOR, PATCH numerically;
- for equal triples, the stable version orders after every pre-release of it;
- among pre-releases of one triple, by N numerically.

So `0.5.1 < 0.6.0-rc1 < 0.6.0-rc2 < 0.6.0 < 0.6.1-rc1`.

## Which release is "previous"

- **Planning a stable version** (any `--bump`, or an explicit stable version) takes the newest *stable* tag as the previous release. Pre-release tags are invisible to it. After `v0.6.0-rc1` exists, a `release:minor` merge still computes `0.6.0` from `v0.5.1`, and a `release:patch` still cuts `0.5.2`. A stable version has to order after the newest stable tag, as today.
- **Planning a pre-release** (an explicit `X.Y.Z-rcN`) has to order after *every* existing release tag, stable or pre-release. So `0.6.0-rc2` follows `0.6.0-rc1`, `0.6.0-rc1` is refused once `v0.6.0` exists, and so is a pre-release below any newer pre-release.

Every script that discovered the previous tag with `git tag --list 'v[0-9]*' --sort=-v:refname | head -n 1` (`plan-release.sh`, `resolve-release-version.sh`, `check-release-changelog.sh`, `cut-release.sh`) discovers it through the shared helper instead, asking for the stable newest or the overall newest as the case above requires.

## The changelog

A pre-release is not a release, so the changelog is not consulted: `plan-release.sh` skips `check-release-changelog.sh` for a pre-release version and says so (`pre-release vX.Y.Z-rcN needs no CHANGELOG entry`). The `## Unreleased` heading stays where it is. The pre-release's GitHub release notes are, in order of preference: the `## Unreleased` section's body when it has one, otherwise generated notes. `changelog-entry.sh` learns to print the Unreleased section when asked for it. A stable release's notes are unchanged.

## What publishes

`publish-release.sh` publishes a pre-release the way it publishes a release, with three differences: the GitHub release is created with `--prerelease`; the notes come from the rule above; and the Homebrew tap is left alone (no formula rendered, no commit, no push), so `brew upgrade` never serves a pre-release. `render-homebrew-formula.sh` refuses a pre-release version outright, as a second line of defense. The rerun check (an existing release must hold exactly the same five assets) is unchanged. `release.sh` builds the same four archives, named with the full version (`workbook_0.6.0-rc1_darwin_arm64.tar.gz`).

`validate-release-tag.sh`, `check-release-published.sh` and `delete-release-tag.sh` accept a pre-release tag; the second already does, and the third gains the recovery path for a pre-release whose workflow failed after tagging.

## How it is cut

Two of the three entrances take an exact version and both accept a pre-release:

- the Actions button: `gh workflow run cut-release.yml -f version=0.6.0-rc1` (the `bump` input is ignored when a version is given, as today; its description says a pre-release is cut this way);
- the checkout: `./scripts/cut-release.sh 0.6.0-rc1`, whose report names the previous stable release and, for a pre-release, says the tap will not be updated.

The release pull request path takes only a label and therefore only cuts stable versions; `release-pr.yml` does not change. `release.yml` does not change either: the tag trigger `v*` already matches, and every decision lives in the scripts it calls.

## Documentation

CONTRIBUTING's Releasing section gains a "Pre-releases" subsection stating the grammar, that only an exact version cuts one, what it publishes and skips, and that the next stable release ignores pre-release tags when computing its version. The "From a checkout" and "The Actions button" subsections mention the form.

## Verification

Every script change carries tests in `scripts/*_test.go`, the way the existing release scripts do: the ordering table above, the previous-tag rules for both cases against a fixture repository with mixed tags, the changelog skip and the Unreleased-notes rule, the `--prerelease` flag and the untouched tap in the publish test's fake `gh` and tap repository, and the formula renderer's refusal. `go test ./scripts` passes, and `./scripts/cut-release.sh 0.6.0-rc1 --dry-run` on main passes every check and stops before tagging.
